standard.title: Collect and record information
standard.description: collect, sort and record information and data from observations and from provided sources, including unscaled timelines and labelled maps or models
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFS02): Students sorted and recorded information using pictorial timelines and located features on pictorial maps or models.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students collect, sort and record information from observations and provided sources, including unscaled timelines and labelled maps.

nodes.label: Collecting from a range of sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collect relevant information from a range of provided sources (stories, photographs, maps, observations) for a HASS inquiry.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect information from at least two different types of sources (e.g. a photograph and an observation) and identify what each source tells them.
nodes.typical_width: Explore stories from the past and present about people, families and places (fiction, letters, diaries, songs, Dreaming stories, films); gather evidence from local observations, aerial photographs and sketches; identify relevant information from each source type.
wider: Compare what different source types (photograph vs oral history vs observation) reveal about the same topic and discuss why sources differ
Identify which sources are primary (from the time) and which are secondary (created later) and discuss why this matters
nodes.hinge_reason: Recording on timelines and maps (Nodes 2–3) requires students to have collected information first — collecting is the prerequisite; without it, there is nothing to record.

response_modes.reason: Year 1 students need to encounter multiple source types before they can select and use them — build a class repertoire through whole-class exploration of each source type.

success_criteria: Collects information from at least two different source types
Identifies at least one piece of relevant information from each source

nodes.label: Recording on unscaled timelines
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sequence events or objects from different generations onto an unscaled timeline in the correct order.
nodes.minimum_width: Place at least three labelled items on an unscaled timeline in correct chronological sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Create a peg timeline or pictorial timeline in which labelled drawn or photographic representations of events or objects from different generations are placed in correct sequence; explain the ordering.
wider: Create a timeline spanning three generations and identify the biggest changes between each generation
Compare two different timelines of the same topic (e.g. toys then and now) and note similarities and differences in what each shows

response_modes.reason: Sequencing on unscaled timelines requires spatial reasoning about time — use physical peg timelines and sorting before moving to drawn timelines.

success_criteria: Places at least three items on a timeline in correct chronological order
Labels each item with a name or drawn representation

nodes.label: Recording on labelled maps
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can record data about locations and features by labelling them on a map of the local area.
nodes.minimum_width: Label at least two features or locations on a provided map (e.g. their home, a local park).
nodes.typical_width: Record data about locations of places and features on maps and plans; label activity spaces on classroom plans; label home location on a map of the local area; record observations of weather and seasons in pictorial form.
wider: Add a layer of classification to a labelled map (e.g. colour-coding natural, managed and constructed features)
Compare a labelled map with an aerial photograph of the same area and identify what each representation shows differently

response_modes.reason: Labelled mapping integrates observation, feature classification and spatial representation — the labelled map is the capstone recording format for Year 1.

success_criteria: Labels at least two features or locations on a provided map
Labels are accurate to the feature's location on the map
